Police Station, Karsog, District Mandi.

Virender Singh, Judge Applicant- Nek Chand has filed the present application, under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.P.C.'), for releasing him on bail,
during the pendency of trial, in case FIR No. 121 of 2023, dated 26.10.2023, registered with Police Station, Karsog, District Mandi, under Section 376 (2) & 506 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'the IPC") and Section 6 of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
(hereinafter referred to as 'the POCSO Act').
2.

entities.text: Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: According to the applicant, he is an innocent person and has falsely been implicated, in this case.
According to him, he and the child victim were in love affair and they wanted to get married.
3. According to the applicant, at the insistence of the child victim, the applicant has married her on 21.10.2023.
In this regard, affidavits have also been executed by the applicant, as well as, the child victim.
The child victim spent about 5 days in the house of the applicant.
However, the parents of the child victim, as well as, her relatives had hatched a conspiracy and lodged the FIR in question.
4. According to him, he is having no criminal antecedents.
5. The applicant, through his counsel, has given certain undertakings, for which he is ready to abide by, in case, ordered to be released on bail.
6. On the basis of above facts, a prayer has been made to allow the present application.

7. When put to notice, the Police filed the status report, disclosing therein that on 25.10.2023, the Nek Chand vs State Of H.P on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14312835/
1 child victim, whose age has been mentioned as 19 years, appeared before the Police, alongwith her parents.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She has made a complaint, disclosing therein that she is 19 years of age.

According to her,
she was sexually exploited by the applicant, for the last three years.

According to her, at that time,
she was 16 years of age and was minor.
The accused had threatened her by saying that in case, she discloses this fact to anybody, he will make the information public of exploiting her sexually.
7.1 According to the child victim, whenever, the child victim failed to attend the phone calls of the applicant and respond to his messages, he used to threatened her.
According to the child victim, the applicant threatened her that he is having such proofs that if he makes them public, then, it will be difficult for the child victim to get out of her house.
The applicant is stated to be the uncle of child victim, in relation.
According to the child victim, due to these tactics, the applicant obtained her signatures, over the affidavits, in Tehsil Karsog, before Notary Public.
When, the child victim refused to do so, the applicant threatened her to make the information viral.
Due to this fact, the child victim had signed the same.
Lastly, the child victim got recorded that applicant had threatened her to eliminate her parents.
8. On the basis of above facts, the Police registered the FIR in question and criminal machinery swung into motion.
The child victim was sent for medico-legal examination and Doctor has preserved the physical evidence.
The applicant was arrested on 26.10.2023.
He was also sent for medico legal examination and physical evidence, so collected, by the Doctor, was sent for chemical analysis to RFSL, Mandi.
9. Other codal formalities were completed, including the fact that the relevant register of oath from the Notary Public was also taken into possession.

10. Lastly, it has been apprehended that in case, the applicant is released on bail, he may coerce the witnesses and allure them to depose in his favour and he may not be available for trial, and his release on bail, will give wrong signal to the society.
11. According to the documents, annexed with the petition, the affidavits were allegedly executed on 21.10.2023, and the FIR in question was registered on 26.10.2023.
This fact will be proved during the trial, whether the documents in question were got signed by the accused by coercion.
12. The role, allegedly played by the applicant, will be proved during the course of the trial.
The application cannot be dismissed as a matter of punishment, as, pre-trial punishment is prohibited under the law.

13. It is no longer res-integra that at the time of deciding the bail-application, detailed discussion about the evidence, so collected by the prosecution, during the investigation, should be avoided, as it would cause prejudice to the case of the applicant, as well as, to the case of the prosecution.
14. The applicant cannot be kept in judicial custody, for indefinite period, as the chances of commencement and conclusion of trial, against the applicant, are not so bright.

2 15.
The applicant is permanent resident of District Mandi, as such, it cannot be apprehended that he may not be available for trial.

16. So far as the apprehensions, which have been expressed by the Police, in the status report, are concerned, those apprehensions are not sufficient to decline the relief to the applicant, for which, he is otherwise entitled to, as, for those apprehensions, reasonable conditions can be imposed, in case,
the applicant is ordered to be released on bail.
17. Considering all these facts, this Court is of the view that the bail application is liable to be allowed and is accordingly allowed.

18. The applicant is ordered to be released on bail in case FIR No. 121 of 2023, dated 26.10.2023,
registered with Police Station, Karsog, District Mandi, under Sections 376 (2) and 506 of the IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act, on his furnishing personal bail bond, in the sum of Rs. 50,000/-, with one surety of the like amount, to the satisfaction of learned CJM Mandi/JMIC Karsog/ any Duty Magistrate, stationed at Mandi.

19. Any of the observations, made hereinabove, shall not be taken as an expression of opinion, on the merits of the case, as these observations, are confined, only, to the disposal of the present bail application.
20. It is made clear that the respondent-State is at liberty to move an appropriate application, in case, any of the bail conditions, is found to be violated by the applicant.

21. The Registry is directed to forward a soft copy of the bail order to the Superintendent of Judicial Lock-up, Karsog through email, with a direction to enter the date of grant of bail in the e-prison software.

22. In case, the applicant is not released within a period of seven days from the date of grant of bail,
the Superintendent of Judicial Lock-up, Karsog, is directed to inform this fact to the Secretary,
